There are two opinions concerning it.

One is that it is Madani; this was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas.

The second is that it is Makki; this was related by Abu Kurayb from Ibn Abbas.

If it is asked: Why did He specify "the people" here by saying that He is their Lord, when He is the Lord of everything?

There are two answers to this.

The first is that they are the honoured ones, distinguished above others.

The second is that when He commanded seeking refuge from their evil, He informed them that He is their Lord, so that they would know that He is the One who protects them from their evil. One is that the whispering into the breasts of mankind comes from their jinn and their men, so He called the jinn here "men," as He called them "men" in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿There were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ [al-Jinn: 6], and called them "a company" in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A company of the jinn listened﴾ [al-Jinn: 1]. The second is that the whisperer who whispers into the breasts of mankind is of the jinn, and they are of the jinn. The meaning is: from the evil of the whisperer who is of the jinn. Then His saying, the Exalted, "and mankind," is joined to "al-waswas." The meaning is: from the evil of the whisperer, and from the evil of mankind, as if he were commanded to seek refuge from both the jinn and mankind. This is the opinion of al-Zajjaj.
